record.original_question: For a finite function-symbol set containing at least one associative-commutative function symbol, let T be the set of ground terms modulo the AC axioms. Is the Sigma-2 fragment of the first-order theory of T decidable, especially the complement problem asking whether a term has an instance not matching any of a finite family of other terms modulo AC?

evidence.quote: Is the Σ2-fragment of the first-order theory of ground terms modulo AC decidable?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite set of function symbols containing at least one designated binary symbol $+$ that is assumed to be associative and commutative; let $AC$ denote the equational theory consisting of the axioms
$$x+(y+z) = (x+y)+z, \qquad x+y = y+x.$$
Let $T(\mathcal{F})$ be the set of ground terms built from $\mathcal{F}$ and let $T(\mathcal{F})/{=_{AC}}$ be its quotient by the congruence generated by $AC$. Consider the first-order structure whose domain is $T(\mathcal{F})/{=_{AC}}$ and whose signature consists of the function symbols of $\mathcal{F}$, interpreted as the operations on $AC$-equivalence classes.

The $\Sigma_2$ fragment of the first-order theory of this structure consists of all closed formulas of the form
$$\exists \bar{x}\, \forall \bar{y}\, \varphi(\bar{x},\bar{y}),$$
where $\varphi$ is a quantifier-free formula in the language of $\mathcal{F}$ (with equality).

Question: Is the $\Sigma_2$ fragment of this first-order theory decidable? In particular, is the following "complement problem" decidable: given terms $t, t_1, \dots, t_n$ over $\mathcal{F}$ (possibly with variables), decide whether there exists a ground instance of $t$ that is not $AC$-equal to any ground instance of any $t_i$?
artifact.status_search_result: The linear AC-complement problem (and certain restricted non-linear classes) is known to be decidable through tree-automata techniques (Kounalis–Lugiez, Comon–Jacquemard, and others). However, satisfiability for the general non-linear AC-complement problem remains open, and consequently the decidability of the full $\Sigma_2$ fragment of the first-order theory of ground terms modulo AC is not established. The question therefore appears partially solved.

status_evidence.title: AC Complement Problems: Satisfiability and Negation Elimination
status_evidence.snippet: Negation elimination is decidable for linear complement problems interpreted in T(F)/=AC; for non-linear AC-complement problems even satisfiability is an open problem, though decidable for a particular class where variables do not occur directly below AC-function symbols.
status_evidence.claim: Linear AC-complement problem is decidable; general non-linear case open.

status_evidence.title: Complement problems and tree automata in AC-like theories
status_evidence.snippet: Reduces the complement problem modulo a theory to recognition by tree automata closed under union and complementation; answered for linear terms in AC-like theories.
status_evidence.claim: Tree-automata approach yields decidability for linear AC-complement problems.

status_evidence.title: A solution of the complement problem in associative-commutative theories
status_evidence.snippet: Provides a solution of the complement problem in AC theories.
status_evidence.claim: Partial positive results exist for AC complement problem.
